Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Las Vegas NV
349 AM PST Tue Nov 17 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Showers and gusty winds will continue into the afternoon, with 
  conditions improving overnight as the low exits the region.

* A second, colder system will bring another round of unsettled  
  weather to the region during the second half of the week. 

* Unsettled weather will continue into next week as the weather 
  pattern remains active.

&&

.DISCUSSION...through Monday.

Current water vapor and infrared satellite imagery show a trough 
pushing into southeastern California and southern Nevada. This 
trough is responsible for the ongoing shower activity across 
southeastern California, southern Nevada, and northwestern 
Arizona. Showers will continue through mid-to-late morning, with 
activity quickly dropping off behind the trough axis. Moderate 
rain, ponding of water in low lying areas, and a lightning strike 
or two will be the primary concerns with these storms as they move
through. Gusty westerly-to-southwesterly winds will pick up 
across the Mojave Desert during the early morning hours as the 
base of the trough swings through the area. These gusty winds will
continue across the Mojave Desert through late this afternoon. 
Blowing dust, unsecured items blowing away, and difficult driving 
conditions for high profile vehicles will be the primary concerns 
with these winds today.

A stronger, colder system will follow on the heels of today's 
system, bringing another round of cool, unsettled weather to the 
region Wednesday through Friday. This system will bring heavy 
mountain snow to the Eastern Sierra, where the Winter Storm Watch 
has been upgraded to a Winter Storm Warning. Storm total snow 
amounts will be around 22 to 32 inches in Aspendell, CA (elevation
8,400 feet), with a higher end amount of 36 inches. Precipitation
will spill over the Eastern Sierra, with moderate mountain snow 
expected in the White Mountains of Inyo County. A Winter Weather 
Advisory is in effect for the White Mountains from Wednesday 
morning through Friday morning. Storm total snow amounts through 
Westgard Pass are expected to be around 3 to 8 inches with a 
higher end scenario of 12 inches possible (10% chance of higher 
end scenario). Outside of Eastern Sierra and White Mountains, 
showers will gradually spread eastward throughout the day 
Wednesday into Thursday before clearing out on Friday. Mountain 
snow will be possible in the higher terrain of southern Nevada 
into northwestern Arizona with snow levels starting out around 
6,000 to 7,000 feet on Wednesday, eventually falling to around 
5,000 feet as the trough axis swings through early Friday morning.
Lower elevations will see increased chances for light-to-moderate
rain showers on Wednesday and Thursday, with the "heaviest" lower
elevation/valley precipitation expected to occur in the Owens 
Valley. The primary concerns with Wednesday and Thursday's rain 
will be ponding of water in low lying areas, nuisance flooding, 
and slick, wet roadways.

Conditions will improve Friday afternoon into Saturday as the  
trough exits the region. Weak, transient ridging will set up 
across the area on Saturday, providing a brief reprieve from 
unsettled weather before the next looks to impact region early 
next week as the weather pattern remains active.

&&

.AVIATION...For Harry Reid...For the 12Z Forecast
Package...Scattered showers will continue in the Las Vegas Valley
through mid-morning, with the most likely time frame for impacts 
at the terminal within the first couple hours of the forecast 
period. Brief periods with ceilings around 3-5kft are expected 
with passing showers, with a rapid improvement in ceilings 
expected through the morning as showers move east. VFR conditions 
are expected to return by late morning into early afternoon, with 
cloud bases remaining at or above 15kft thereafter. Southwesterly 
winds will become gusty later this morning, with sustained speeds
around 15-18KT and gusts to 25-30KT expected through mid- 
afternoon, when winds gradually diminish. After sunset, light 
winds resume, veering from the southwest to northwest.


For the rest of southern Nevada, northwest Arizona and southeast
California...For the 12Z Forecast Package...Bands of showers are
moving eastward across the area at issuance, expected to progress
east of area terminals by mid- morning. Showers are most likely 
to impact Las Vegas Valley and Lower Colorado River Valley 
terminals early in the forecast period, with lower ceilings to 
2-4kft expected with passing showers, and brief visibility 
reductions in areas of heavier rain. As showers move east, 
ceilings will quickly improve, with VFR conditions returning 
areawide by late morning into early afternoon. Gusty southwesterly
winds develop areawide by mid-morning, with gusts to 20-30KT 
expected, with the exception of KBIH in the northern Owens Valley 
where winds remain northerly, and from KIFP to KEED, where 
sheltering will limit gust potential. Additionally, stronger 
westerly gusts to around 35KT are expected across the western 
Mojave Desert/KDAG this morning through mid-afternoon. Winds 
become light after sunset.

&&

.SPOTTER INFORMATION STATEMENT...Spotters are encouraged to report
any significant weather or impacts according to standard operating
procedures.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Stessman 
AVIATION...Phillipson

For more forecast information...see us on our webpage:
https://weather.gov/lasvegas or follow us on Facebook and Twitter
